claims.text: every line carries the SHA of the line before it
claims.why: `_entry_sha` computes SHA-256 of (prev + '\0' + body_sha + '\0' + ts); prev is the previous entry_sha.

claims.text: TAIL truncation (any prefix of a valid chain is itself a valid chain) is caught only against the head/count ANCHOR persisted beside the transcript
claims.why: `anchor_path` defines the anchor file path, but the verification logic is not present in this chunk.

claims.text: It deliberately REIMPLEMENTS memstore.py's two-SHA discipline instead of importing it
claims.why: `_body_sha` and `_entry_sha` are defined locally; no import from memstore is present.

claims.text: it must never write to the memory ledger
claims.why: `_resolve_store` raises ValueError if the resolved path is under `_FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR`.

claims.text: COUNCIL RECORDS ARE NEVER AN INPUT TO MEMORY RECALL
claims.why: No code in this chunk enforces that council records are excluded from memory recall; that logic would be elsewhere.

claims.text: Any store path under `<repo>/memory/` is refused loudly by `_resolve_store`
claims.why: `_resolve_store` raises ValueError if the path is under `_FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR`.

claims.text: body_sha -- sha256 over json.dumps(canonical_body, sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":"), ensure_ascii=True)
claims.why: `_body_sha` calls `hashlib.sha256(canonical_body_json(...).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()` and `canonical_body_json` uses the exact parameters.

claims.text: canonical_body is the record MINUS the four position/identity fields ts, prev, entry_sha, id (and body_sha itself)
claims.why: `canonical_body` filters out keys in `_NON_BODY_FIELDS`, which includes 'ts', 'prev', 'entry_sha', 'id', 'body_sha'.

claims.text: entry_sha -- sha256(prev + "\0" + body_sha + "\0" + ts), the chain link. Genesis prev is None and folds in as ""
claims.why: `_entry_sha` computes `(prev or '') + '\0' + body_sha + '\0' + ts` and returns its SHA-256.

claims.text: a turn's id is entry_sha[:16], not body_sha[:16]
claims.why: The assignment of `id` is not in this chunk; the claim refers to logic elsewhere.

claims.text: there is NO dedupe
claims.why: No deduplication logic is present or referenced in this chunk.

claims.text: append_round takes a whole round's turns in ANY completion order, sorts them by the vendor-namespaced actor id, assigns seq at chain time, and stamps ONE chain timestamp for the round
claims.why: `append_round` is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: sensitivity.secret_floor_rule has two independent channels and they are fed SEPARATELY here
claims.why: `_scan_paths` calls `secret_floor_rule(str(p), '')` and `_scan_texts` calls `secret_floor_rule('', str(t))`; the path and content channels are separate.

claims.text: PATH channel: every evidence path, INDIVIDUALLY
claims.why: `_scan_paths` iterates over paths and calls `secret_floor_rule` on each one individually.

claims.text: CONTENT channel: the turn content, every ref, and every metadata string, each scanned on its own -- never over the assembled turn
claims.why: `_scan_texts` iterates over texts and calls `secret_floor_rule` on each individually; `_meta_strings` extracts string values from meta.

claims.text: This runs on OUTBOUND turns and, critically, on INBOUND vendor responses BEFORE they are chained: once a secret is inside a hash-chained line it can never be redacted without breaking verify_chain
claims.why: The timing of when the scan runs (before chaining) is not specified in this chunk.

claims.text: A hit REFUSES the turn -- no redact-and-send, no redact-and-store. In its place a status="refused" receipt is chained naming ONLY the rule label
claims.why: The logic for handling a hit (refusing the turn and creating a receipt) is not in this truncated chunk; `_scan_turn` is incomplete.

claims.text: The receipt is re-scanned before it is written; if the identity fields themselves carry the secret the receipt degrades to an anonymous one
claims.why: No receipt creation or re-scanning logic is visible in this chunk.

claims.text: ONE CARVE-OUT, DELIBERATE: `withheld` (paths an egress lane declined to send) is scanned with the CONTENT channel only, never the path channel.
claims.why: The handling of `withheld` is not present in this chunk.

claims.text: EVERY REQUESTED PARTICIPANT PRODUCES EXACTLY ONE CHAINED TURN PER ROUND
claims.why: The logic ensuring exactly one turn per participant per round is not in this chunk.

claims.text: A turn is one of these and nothing else. There is deliberately no "ok" here: a status value that reads as a verdict is one grep away from becoming one.
claims.why: `TURN_STATUS` includes only 'spoke', 'refused', 'unavailable', 'budget_exhausted', 'anomaly'; 'ok' is absent.

claims.text: Machine reasons -- fixed vocabulary, so "why is this council degraded?" is answerable by a filter and not by reading prose.
claims.why: `UNAVAILABLE_REASONS` and `ANOMALY_REASONS` are tuples of fixed string constants.

claims.text: Fail-closed ceiling on a single turn. Transcript tokens grow as O(V^2 R^2), not O(V R); the per-council budget lives in session.py, but no single turn may blow the file up on its own.
claims.why: `MAX_CONTENT_CHARS = 200_000` enforces a per-turn limit.

claims.text: ADR-010 actor-namespace rule, pinned to the MODEL and not just the vendor: "claude said X" is not reproducible six months out, because the model behind a stable command name changes underneath it.
claims.why: `_ACTOR_RE` regex enforces the pattern `council.<vendor>.<model>`.

claims.text: Position/identity fields, excluded from body_sha (see module docstring).
claims.why: `_NON_BODY_FIELDS` includes 'ts', 'prev', 'entry_sha', 'id', 'body_sha'.

claims.text: Accepted caller keys. A key outside this set is REFUSED loudly, never dropped: a silently dropped field lets two semantically distinct turns canonicalise to the same body and hands the caller a success id for a turn never recorded.
claims.why: `_ALLOWED_TURN_KEYS` is defined; the refusal logic is not in this chunk but the set is present.

claims.text: Per-store append index: tail entry_sha + record/turn counts, keyed by resolved path and invalidated by the file's (size, mtime_ns). Re-parsing the whole transcript per append is O(n^2) overall; a 500-turn council must not pay that.
claims.why: `_APPEND_CACHE` dict is defined; intended use is described in comment.

claims.text: The content projection body_sha is taken over: everything EXCEPT the position/identity fields. Uniform across turn and roster records so the chain walk needs no per-record-type branch.
claims.why: `canonical_body` filters out `_NON_BODY_FIELDS`; no type-specific logic.

claims.text: The exact bytes hashed. Exposed so a test can assert determinism against the canonical form rather than against a digest it cannot inspect.
claims.why: Function returns JSON string; deterministic due to `sort_keys=True`, fixed separators, `ensure_ascii=True`.

claims.text: council.<vendor>.<model> per ADR-010. An unknown model id is recorded as the literal unknown by the CALLER -- never omitted, never inferred.
claims.why: Returns `f'council.{vendor}.{model}'`; no inference logic.

claims.text: One evidence citation: the path as given plus the sha256 of the exact bytes shown to the model. Two participants citing "the file" may have been shown different bytes; without this the transcript records a citation that cannot be reproduced.
claims.why: Returns dict with 'path' (normalized) and 'sha256' (SHA-256 of data).

claims.text: <base_dir>/<council_id>.jsonl. council_id is filename-safe by validation, not by sanitising: a silently rewritten id would point two councils at one transcript.
claims.why: Calls `_check_council_id` which validates against regex; no sanitization.

claims.text: The head/count anchor beside the transcript. Separate file on purpose: the chain walk cannot detect tail truncation from a truncated file alone.
claims.why: Returns path with '.anchor.json' appended to filename; separate file.

claims.text: Resolve and REFUSE any path under <repo>/memory/. Council turns must never reach the memory ledger (see module docstring).
claims.why: Raises ValueError if resolved path is under `_FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR`.

claims.text: PATH channel, one path at a time -- so a hit is attributable to one path and a diff that ADDS .env cannot hide inside a blob.
claims.why: Iterates over paths and calls `secret_floor_rule` on each individually.

claims.text: CONTENT channel, one string at a time. path="" here is correct and is NOT the forbidden whole-prompt call: the path tier is run separately over every evidence path above, so it is never skipped.
claims.why: Iterates over texts and calls `secret_floor_rule('', str(t))`; path channel is separate.

observations.what: The module docstring makes many claims about runtime behavior (e.g., refusal receipts, withheld carve-out, per-round sequencing) that are not verifiable in this chunk. These claims depend on functions not yet defined (append_round, _scan_turn completion, write logic).
_scan_turn is truncated; its full implementation is needed to verify claims about refusal receipts and the withheld carve-out.
